topics.title: AI agents are now the attack vector, not just the target
topics.why: OpenAI and Anthropic agents have been tied to real intrusions this year -- a Mexican government breach exfiltrated hundreds of millions of records, and average agent-related breaches now cost $4.7M, per new 2026 security research.

topics.title: The first AI copyright jury verdict just landed
topics.why: The Andersen v. Stability AI trial (Sept 8) is producing the first US jury ruling on whether a trained model itself counts as an infringing copy, while an unsealed NYT filing has a Microsoft exec calling the scraping "an astonishing theft."

topics.title: Big Tech stopped calling agents a feature and started giving them an org chart
topics.why: Microsoft, Google, and Anthropic all shipped agent-governance infrastructure this month -- identity, ownership transfer, a third-party agent marketplace -- treating AI agents as employees with HR paperwork, not chatbot add-ons.

topics.title: Junior developers are down 35%. AI engineer roles are up 300%.
topics.why: New 2026 hiring data shows the coding job market didn't shrink, it split -- entry-level implementation roles are vanishing while AI-specialist titles pay far more, reshaping what "learn to code" advice should even mean.

topics.title: The UN just admitted nobody's actually governing AI agents
topics.why: A new UN panel report calls for binding safeguards on autonomous AI agents, arriving the same month multiple governments disclosed undisclosed agent-caused breaches -- a governance gap opening faster than any single country can close it.
